newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao cleared in forgery case - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao cleared in forgery case - lawyer.

text.p: An Indian judge on Wednesday dropped charges against former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in a forgery trial, one of three criminal cases which had forced him to quit last year as Congress party leader, his lawyer said.

Judge Ajit Bharihoke dismissed the government's claim that Rao had been involved in an attempt in 1989 to defame V.P. Singh, an opposition leader who later became prime minister, lawyer R.K. Anand said.
"The judge has discharged Mr Narasimha Rao, saying there was no evidence of conspiracy," Anand told Reuters by telephone after the judge's ruling.
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the federal police agency, had accused Rao and three others of conspiring to smear Singh for political ends.
The case involved the alleged falsification of bank documents to show that Singh's son, Ajeya Singh, had a secret bank account with $21 million on the Caribbean island of St Kitts.
At the time V.P. Singh, who had left the then ruling Congress party for the opposition, was spearheading an anti-corruption campaign against the government.

V.P. Singh became prime minister at the end of 1989 after Congress lost general elections. Authorities later cleared Ajeya Singh of allegations that he had violated foreign exchange and anti-corruption laws.

Last year the CBI indicted Rao, former minister K.K. Tiwari, Hindu guru Chandraswami and an aide of criminal conspiracy, forgery, giving false evidence and using forged documents. The charges carry a maximum sentence of seven years in jail.
Rao's lawyers later argued their client, who was foreign minister at the time of the alleged forgery, had acted on the orders of the office of then prime minister Rajiv Gandhi.
Gandhi was killed by a suicide bomber in 1991 during a general election campaign.
Bharihoke also cleared Tiwari but indicted Chandraswami and his aide for criminal conspiracy and forgery, Anand said.
A CBI spokesman said the agency would review the judge's decision before deciding whether to file an appeal.
Rao served as prime minister for five years until his Congress party suffered its worst defeat in general elections last year.
Widely credited with opening India to foreign investment and trade, Rao was hobbled at the end of his term by allegations of corruption.
He has been indicted in two other cases, one involving alleged criminal fraud and the other vote-buying.
Rao, who has said he is innocent in the cases, was forced to step down as Congress party president last September to face trial.
A hearing in the fraud case, which also involves Chandraswami, has been set for July 3, while arguments in the vote-for-bribes trial will be made on August 8, Anand said.
